clue.text: Nonsense surrounding public transport being in a healthy state

indicators.note: the nonsense word goes round the outside of the transport word, enclosing it

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish talk
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A complaint that the bus network is somehow both rubbish and in fine shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust describes something strong and vigorous, a synonym for being in good health.

clue.text: Right tone perhaps, to suppress information on scale of radiation

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, so in this down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the information
perhaps suggests the word tone might be another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Advice about keeping quiet on radiation readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is a unit for measuring exposure to X-ray and gamma radiation.

clue.text: Races in to purchase something to eat

indicators.note: the races abbreviation goes inside the purchase word

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Someone dashing in to buy a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUTTY is northern English slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A butty is an informal British word for a sandwich, a snack.

clue.text: Earl's reformed around two thousand in prison

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the roman numerals
reformed means formed again, so the letters of the earl's word are rearranged

parts.note: the word earl plus its S, used as letters
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who has mended his ways while in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges the earl's letters to SLAER, and 'around' wraps that round two Roman thousands; the possessive S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Slammer is slang for prison.

clue.text: Accepts there's trouble with the points

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing
PTS is the standard abbreviation for points

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to trouble over a scoreboard tally.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a proposal or idea is to accept and take it on as your own.

clue.text: In reality, fed up with scenes on love

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
an act of a play is made up of scenes
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone truly sick of romantic scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for in fact, existing in reality whether or not legally.

clue.text: Flowers can make proper wines

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
rosés are pink wines

explanation.surface: Advice that bottles can make good wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Primroses are pale yellow spring flowers.

clue.text: The odds on whip getting wet

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: A jockey whipping a horse in the rain on race day.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash someone is to wet them with spattered liquid.

clue.text: The physical consequence of a passion that's reckless?

parts.note: heat is strong passion or intensity of feeling
rash means hasty and reckless

explanation.surface: A wry question about what reckless passion does to the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat rash is a skin irritation, a bodily effect brought on by being too hot.

clue.text: The sort of existence crew have to speak of silently?

parts.note: a hand is a crew member on a ship
taken as written
to mouth words is to form them with the lips without sound

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of life sailors lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Living hand to mouth is a precarious existence, spending earnings immediately with nothing saved.

clue.text: Horse crossing river gets ruffled

indicators.note: the horse word goes across, and so around, the river abbreviation

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A horse wading over a river comes out flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is trimmed with ruffles, gathered strips of fabric.

clue.text: Answer in pen, but check

indicators.note: the answer abbreviation is placed inside the pen word

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
A is the abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A

explanation.surface: An exam instruction to write in ink and then check your work.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay something, such as an execution, is to check or halt it.

clue.text: One gets paid to provide fair handed treatment

definitions.text: One gets paid to provide fair handed treatment

parts.words: One gets paid to provide fair handed treatment
parts.note: fair-handed suggests even-handed justice, but read literally it is paid work that makes hands look fair and neat

explanation.surface: A description of an impartial professional, like a judge or arbitrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair handed' reads as 'even-handed', but here it means treatment that leaves the hands fair, that is, nicely groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicurist is paid to tidy and beautify clients' hands and nails.

clue.text: Share in famous people's festivities

indicators.note: the share word sits inside the famous people word

parts.note: celebs are famous people, celebrities
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Joining in the parties of the famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrations are festivities held to mark a happy occasion.

clue.text: Came off a diet — perhaps too thin?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone off, gone wrong, and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone who quit a diet, wondering whether they had got too thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin and wasted, an extreme sense of too thin.

clue.text: Condemn the little weight given to study

indicators.note: the little weight is given, added on, to the end of the study

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Criticism that a study carries little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly.

clue.text: Achieved success, being highly skilled

definitions.meaning: something ... has been brought off or completed successfully
an ... performer is expert and talented

explanation.surface: Praise for someone both successful and talented.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished means both completed with success and expert, a double sense of the word.

clue.text: Horse power thus restored?

definitions.meaning: a battery ... restores power to a flat device

explanation.surface: A horse that recovers its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Charger means both a war horse and a device restoring electrical power.

clue.text: Old wine is different — it has to rest

indicators.note: is different means the letters of old wine take another order

explanation.surface: Aged wine tastes different and should be left to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline and rest.

clue.text: Friend with service in royal house

parts.note: a pal is a friend
an ace is an unreturned serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A friend serving in the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence of a monarch.

clue.text: Representation from a recruit worried by external criteria

indicators.note: external picks the outside letters, first and last, of the word criteria
worried letters are shaken about, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new recruit fretting about being judged by outside standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'external' gives C and A, the first and last letters of criteria; 'worried' mixes them with A RECRUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is an exaggerated representation of a person, typically a drawing.

clue.text: Post traumatic situation

indicators.note: traumatic suggests the word post has been through a shock that jumbles it

explanation.surface: A clinical phrase, as in post-traumatic stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the phrase 'post-traumatic'; split it and 'traumatic' rearranges POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or position, and a tight spot is a difficult situation.

clue.text: Prophet offering protection for women's outlet

indicators.note: the prophet word surrounds and shields the women abbreviation

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A prophet sheltering women, offering them an outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is a drain, an outlet for waste water.

clue.text: Label attached to tabloid for the rabble

indicators.note: attached to puts the label word after the tabloid word

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging name for a low-quality newspaper
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A tabloid branding the masses as a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, means a disreputable mob, the riff-raff.

clue.text: Gangster confronting flash fool

indicators.note: confronting means standing face to face, so the gangster comes first, in front of the flash

parts.note: hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster
a wink is a flash, an instant, as in in a wink

explanation.surface: A mobster facing a sudden flash of light, perhaps a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to deceive or trick someone, to make a fool of them.

clue.text: Last to finish university? Engineers!

parts.note: end is a finish
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A jibe that engineers are always the last to finish their degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to last or keep going over time.

clue.text: A French right to be wrong

parts.note: un is French for a
true means right or correct

explanation.surface: An observation that a French entitlement can be mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means false, not correct, so wrong.
